subject: DPA: retention tier exception & erase activation flow

Subject: DPA: retention tier exception & erase activation flow

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a concrete operational flow for the retention/erase scenario you flagged (archive tier exception + immediate erase activation) so your legal and ops teams can review. High level: we support tiered retention (hot / warm / cold archive) and can trigger a customer-initiated erase that propagates through primary, cached prefixes, and snapshot pointers. The key constraints are backup restore windows and third-party snapshot replication (if enabled).

Attached is a short playbook (redwood-erase-playbook-draft.pdf) and a mapping of the data surfaces we see for Acme (acme-data-map.xlsx). The proposal below is intended to be DPA-friendly language that preserves your need for certified erasure while being operationally achievable:

- Erase activation: customer requests erase via support + signed request (DocuSign), Redwood begins workflow within 2 business days.
- Primary data: deleted or irreversibly de-referenced within 10 business days; metadata tombstones may persist for audit for up to 90 days.
- Snapshot/backups: pointers and full backups removed or rotated according to backup retention policy; proof-of-delete certification provided when full removal complete (target 30 business days for backups that cross-region).
- Logs & telemetry: redact personal data on access logs where applicable; operational logs retained 90 days for incident and compliance evidence.

Questions for you/Acme legal:
1) Is the 10/30/90 cadence acceptable as a baseline?
2) Do you need an explicit onshore-only wipe guarantee (we can offer onshore snapshot rotation for an addendum)?
3) Any additional certification language you require (format / minimum contents of the proof-of-erasure)?

If that looks reasonable, I can share a short redline for the DPA (suggested clause language) and we can set a short call with Marissa and Karthik to finalize operational knobs (onshore escrow, BYOK scope, and evidence delivery).

Thanks —

Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: DPA: retention tier exception & erase activation flow

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary and the playbook. A few items from legal/infosec we need to confirm before we proceed to a redline:

- Certification content: we require a signed certificate of erasure that lists: (a) scope of data erased (tenant id, table/object keys), (b) timeline of actions, (c) confirmation that backups/snapshots containing the data have been addressed and the expected completion window, and (d) contact for escalation.
- Backup timelines: 30 business days for backup pointer rotation is long for us unless we can get a firm guarantee on onshore-only snapshots for Acme data (all backups that include Acme must be kept within the US; if replication to other regions is enabled we need that disabled for this tenant).
- Proof delivery: we need the certificate and a downloadable report (CSV) of affected object IDs.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood commit to providing the certificate within 10 business days of completion of the primary erase step (even if backups are still being rotated)? Our auditors treat that as the formal evidence.
2) If onshore-only snapshots are an add-on, what is the cost / lead time?

If you can send a DPA clause that implements the certificate language and clarifies the onshore snapshot option, legal will take a look and likely propose minor redlines. Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

—Sophie

Subject: Re: DPA: retention tier exception & erase activation flow

Thanks Sophie — very helpful. Quick replies inline and then a proposed clause below.

- Certificate: yes, we can produce a signed certificate of erasure. We typically include scope (tenant id, data classes), timeline, actions taken, and the operations contact. We can include a CSV export of affected object ids as requested.
- 10-business-day certificate: operationally we can commit to issuing the certificate within 10 business days from completion of the primary data deletion step. We will note in the certificate whether backups are still in process and their expected completion dates — we cannot issue a certificate that claims backed-up copies are fully removed until that process completes.
- Onshore snapshots: we can offer an onshore-only snapshot rotation option as an addendum; lead time to enable is 5 business days post-signature and it carries a modest monthly fee. That can be scoped to your tenant.

Proposed DPA clause (suggested redline language you can drop into the draft):

"Erase activation and certification. Upon receipt of a duly authorized erase request from Customer, Redwood will initiate the erase workflow within two (2) business days. Primary customer data will be permanently deleted or irreversibly de-referenced within ten (10) business days following workflow initiation. Redwood will provide Customer with a signed Certificate of Erasure that enumerates the scope of deleted data, timestamps for each deletion action, the name and contact of the Redwood operations lead, and an export of affected object identifiers (CSV).

For backups and snapshots that include Customer Data, Redwood will identify any backup copies and provide an estimated completion date for removal or rotation thereof; full removal of backup copies may require up to thirty (30) business days depending on backup windowing and replication, subject to the parties\" mutual agreement. If Customer elects an onshore-only snapshot rotation addendum, Redwood will confine backup retention and rotation activities to the Customer\"s specified jurisdiction for the duration set forth in the addendum.

Operational notes: we will retain minimal audit metadata (tombstones) for up to ninety (90) days solely for incident and legal compliance; such metadata will not contain customer PII.

Let me know if that covers the asks and whether you want the redline in Track Changes. If you’re good, Marissa can draft a clean addendum for the onshore option and Karthik can confirm the security artefacts we’ll include with the certificate.

Jordan

Thanks — jumping in with a slightly tightened clause and an operational checklist that we can attach as an appendix to the DPA. I kept the spirit of Jordan\"s language but made the certification and timeline language explicit to reduce ambiguity:

Suggested DPA clause (final draft for review):

"6. Erase Activation; Certification; Backups
6.1 Erase Activation. Upon receipt of a Customer-authorized erase request, Redwood will begin the erase workflow within two (2) business days.
6.2 Primary Data Deletion. Redwood will delete or irreversibly de-reference Primary Customer Data within ten (10) business days of workflow initiation.
6.3 Certificate of Erasure. Within ten (10) business days following completion of the Primary Data Deletion step, Redwood will deliver to Customer a signed Certificate of Erasure that includes: (a) Customer tenant identifier(s); (b) list of data classes and object identifiers affected; (c) timestamped actions taken; (d) Redwood operations contact for verification; and (e) any outstanding backup remediation steps and expected completion dates.
6.4 Backups and Snapshots. Redwood will identify backup copies and provide an estimated completion date for their removal or rotation; completion of backup removal may take up to thirty (30) business days depending on backup cycles and replication. If Customer elects a jurisdictional backup addendum, Redwood will confine backup retention and rotation activities to the specified jurisdiction as set forth in the addendum.
6.5 Audit Metadata. Redwood may retain minimal non-PII tombstones and audit records for up to ninety (90) days for legal and incident response purposes.

Operational appendix (summary checklist to attach):
- DocuSign/authorized request receipt confirmation (T+0)
- Primary delete complete (target T+10 business days)
- Certificate issued (within 10 business days after primary delete)
- Backup rotation/complete (target T+30 business days)
- CSV export of affected object IDs attached to Certificate

Next steps: If Acme agrees to the clause, we will: 1) add the jurisdictional backup addendum language (pricing/lead time); 2) have Karthik generate a sample certificate template and the CSV schema; and 3) security will provide the verification contact.
